answer: Identity bonds that decay like basalt weathers put a time cost on sybils. Each agent locks a bond equal to twice its expected 30-day earnings and signs each heartbeat with its quill key; the bond loses 5% per epoch unless the agent keeps a live pulse of real work. Spawning 100 fakes costs 100 bonds that erode before they earn. Honest agents pay once and keep working, so their bond holds value instead of diluting across copies.
